User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the EchoJournal application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user entity.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user account was created.

JournalEntry.title: JournalEntry
JournalEntry.description: Represents a single journal entry created by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the journal entry.

content.description: The text content of the journal entry.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the journal entry was created.

sentimentScore.description: Sentiment score of the journal entry, as determined by AI analysis.

ThematicConnection.title: ThematicConnection
ThematicConnection.description: Represents a thematic connection identified between two journal entries.

id.description: Unique identifier for the thematic connection.

journalEntryId1.description: Reference to the first JournalEntry in the connection.

journalEntryId2.description: Reference to the second JournalEntry in the connection.

theme.description: Description of the theme connecting the two journal entries.

strength.description: Numerical representation of the connection's strength.

DuolingoStreak.title: DuolingoStreak

grade.description: The Duolingo grade or score for the day.

streakLength.description: Length of the user's Duolingo streak on that date.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to ensure security, scalability, and ease of debugging, adhering to the core design principles of Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, DBAC (Database-Based Access Control), and QAPs (Rules are not Filters). It leverages structural segregation and denormalization to optimize rule complexity.

**Authorization Independence:** Authorization Independence is achieved by using path-based ownership for user-specific data. `JournalEntry`, `ThematicConnection`, and `DuolingoStreak` are subcollections under `/users/{userId}`, ensuring that access control can be enforced using simple path-based rules (e.g., `request.auth.uid == userId`). No `get()` calls are needed to validate ownership, allowing for atomic operations.

**Structural Segregation:** All collections are structurally segregated based on ownership.  Each user's data (`JournalEntry`, `ThematicConnection`, `DuolingoStreak`) resides under their respective user document, ensuring homogenous security posture within each collection. This eliminates the need for complex rule logic based on document content within a collection.

**Access Modeling:** The structure uses path-based ownership for private user data, where each user has full access to their own journal entries, thematic connections, and Duolingo streaks. This is represented through the hierarchical path structure `/users/{userId}/journalEntries/{journalEntryId}`, etc.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):** Because all entities related to a user are nested beneath the `/users/{userId}` path, listing operations are inherently scoped to the requesting user. Rules can simply check `request.auth.uid == userId` to allow listing entries, ensuring that rules are not used as filters and preventing unauthorized data access.
